overview.title: 1. Game Overview
overview.body: Bakugan Arena is a strategic turn-based battle game. You place Gate Cards, deploy Bakugans, and play Ability Cards to eliminate your opponent's Bakugans.
overview.objective: Goal: eliminate all 3 opposing Bakugans, or let the opponent's timer run out after Turn 0.

deck.title: 2. Deck vs Match Resources
deck.intro: The deck you build and the resources you can actually spend in a match are not the same.
deck.deckAbilities: Between 3 and 6 normal Ability Cards, plus 0 to 3 exclusive abilities (at least 3 abilities total).
deck.matchBakugans: All 3 Bakugans remain available until eliminated.
deck.matchAbilities: Only 3 Ability Cards can be used for the whole match (exclusives included) — choose carefully which ones to spend.
deck.matchGates: Only 3 Gate Cards can be placed for the whole match, even if your deck has more.

setup.title: 3. Turn 0 — Setup
setup.intro: Before regular play, both players must each place a first Gate Card.
setup.mustPlace: This is mandatory: both timers run in parallel.
setup.timerDraw: If a timer hits 0 during Turn 0, the match ends in a draw (no winner).
setup.after: Once both gates are down, the game enters the neutral phase and turns alternate normally.

victory.title: 4. Victory Conditions
victory.timer: The opponent's timer reaches 0 after Turn 0 (during their turn).

draw.title: 5. Draw Conditions
draw.intro: The match ends in a draw if:
draw.noGates: No more Gate Cards can be placed by either player (and no battle is in progress).
draw.mutualElimination: All Bakugans from both players are eliminated at the same time.

neutral.title: 6. Neutral Phase (No Battle)
neutral.intro: Outside of battle, you usually get one main action per turn. Order and restrictions matter.
neutral.placeGateBody: Can be done first. Does not end the turn: you can still deploy a Bakugan afterward.
neutral.deployBody: Places a Bakugan on a gate. After deploying, you can no longer place a gate this turn. Landing on an opposing Bakugan starts a battle.
neutral.abilityBody: Immediately ends the turn. Costs one of your 3 ability uses for the match.
neutral.attributeBody: Some Bakugans (e.g. Preyas) can change attribute once per presence on the board. This can retrigger synergies with an already-opened reactor.

battle.title: 7. Battle System
battle.intro: A battle starts as soon as two opposing Bakugans share the same Gate Card.
battle.duration: Each battle lasts 2 turns of ability / gate opening.
battle.turn1First: The player who placed their Bakugan last (the attacker) acts first — not the first occupant.
battle.turn1May: On a battle turn, a player may:
battle.turn1Ability: Use an Ability Card (if one is playable in that context).
battle.turn1Gate: Open the Gate Card if they own it, and it is neither already open nor blocked.
battle.turn2Body: The opponent then plays with the same options. After that, the battle resolves.
battle.powerBody: At resolution, each player's total G (power) on the slot is compared. Multiple Bakugans for the same player (Triple / Quartet) add their G together.
battle.whyAttack: Why attack? Going second gives you initiative and often the first chance to open your own gate.

afterBattle.title: 8. After Battle — Board Cleanup
afterBattle.intro: Battles never leave the board frozen. Understanding cleanup prevents nasty surprises.
afterBattle.winners: Winning Bakugans return to hand (they do not stay on the gate).
afterBattle.tie: On a power tie, nobody is eliminated: all Bakugans on the slot return to hand.
afterBattle.gateRemoved: The battle's Gate Card is removed and the slot is reset (free for a new gate).
afterBattle.initiative: The winner usually takes initiative for the next phase.
afterBattle.domainWhy: If no living Bakugan is left to deploy (all are already on the board or eliminated) and no battle is active, the game automatically returns every remaining Bakugan to hand.
afterBattle.domainPurpose: Why? To avoid a softlock: with no Bakugan in reserve, nobody could place, and the match would stall. This is not elimination — only recirculation.

gates.title: 9. Gate Card Types
gates.intro: Not every gate plays the same way. Knowing their roles guides placement.
gates.reactorBody: On open, they often grant a power bonus (e.g. +100 G) to Bakugans whose attribute matches.
gates.characterBody: Double (or heavily boost) the power of Bakugans from the matching family. Ideal for forcing a favorable fight.
gates.commandBody: Special effects (movement, multi-battles, revive, etc.). Some activate automatically at battle end.
gates.trapBody: Strong open effects (often direct elimination or a major swing). When a trap opens, the opponent may sometimes cancel it with a gate-cancel ability before the main effect applies.
gates.openTiming: You can only open your own gate, during battle, if it is not already open or blocked.

abilities.title: 10. Ability Cards
abilities.filter: The game filters abilities automatically: a card that cannot be used in the current context does not appear in your hand.
abilities.unused: Examples: a movement card is hidden if there is no other gate; an enemy-control card is hidden without a valid target.
abilities.exclusiveBody: Tied to a specific Bakugan. Some are only playable in the neutral phase; others only if your Bakugan is (or is not) on the board. They also spend from the 3-use counter.
abilities.persistentBody: Some abilities stay active after use and re-apply when the Bakugan is redeployed (until cancelled or the effect ends).
abilities.ohkoBody: Traps or abilities can eliminate a Bakugan without a G comparison. Protections (vs ability, vs gate, or both) can stop those effects.
abilities.airBattle: Air Battle — Move to another gate. Missing from hand if no other gate exists.
abilities.marionette: Marionette — Control / move enemies. Missing if there is no valid target.

strategic.title: 11. Strategic Notes
strategic.intro: Useful habits once the rules click:
strategic.gate: Place gates to create (or avoid) favorable battles — Character and reactors completely change a trade.
strategic.abilities: Each ability is scarce (3 max): save them for the decisive swing, not the first skirmish.
strategic.attackSecond: Attacking second grants initiative: often better than sitting on an empty gate too early.
strategic.overextend: Filling the board with all your Bakugans can trigger domain cleanup or leave you with no answer.
strategic.traps: Traps are strong but counterable: do not always bank on their raw effect.
strategic.outro: Victory comes from timing: positioning, gate opens, and ability-counter management.

help.title: 12. Need Help?
help.discord: Rules questions? Join our Discord — players and staff can help.
help.refresh: If something breaks mid-match, try refreshing the page first — that fixes most temporary issues.
help.report: If it persists or you find a bug, report it on Discord so we can fix it quickly.
help.thanks: Thanks for playing Bakugan Arena, and most importantly:
help.outro: Have fun and enjoy your battles!
